_info.comment: EIP-140's REVERT as a pure function of its inputs: a body of bytecode, a gas budget and a stated rule set go in; the gas the invocation consumed, how it ended and what it handed back come out. No chain id, no height, no upgrade label, no state root.
_info.whyThisIsAComponentAndNotANetworkFixture: The rule set is a per-vector INPUT rather than a schedule position. `networks/ethereumclassic/mainnet/state/gas/` asks WHERE IN THIS CHAIN'S SCHEDULE a number changes; this file asks WHAT THE NUMBER IS and WHICH PROPOSAL CHANGES IT. Neither answers the other's question.
_info.whatThisShapeAssertsThatAStateFixtureCAN: The number itself. A state fixture measuring gas has to store the measurement and assert a state ROOT over it -- `sload_cost.json` runs `GAS SLOAD POP GAS SWAP1 SUB SSTORE` and hashes the result -- so the gas figure is inside a hash and a failing consumer learns only that some root moved. Here the figure is published, and so is the outcome that a root cannot express at all.
_info.theUNITisASHORTBODYandNOTONEOPCODE: An opcode cannot be executed without operands and the operands cost gas, so the measurable thing is always a body. That is also upstream's answer: `ethereum/execution-specs`' CodeGasMeasure wraps a fragment in `GAS ... GAS SWAP1 SUB` and subtracts a stated overhead. This file does not subtract anything -- it publishes the whole body's cost and pairs vectors that differ in one place, so the overhead cancels in the READER's subtraction rather than in the generator's.
_info.oracle: ethereum/go-ethereum's `evm run`, EXECUTED, one invocation per vector, configured by a genesis chain-config fragment.
_info.oracle-version: reference-material/ethereum/go-ethereum at e9e35a42f (branch master), reporting version 1.17.6-unstable-e9e35a42-20260826. Third-party upstream work -- never fukuii, which these fixtures exist to certify, and never a repo under work/repos/, which on this machine is the maintainer's own.
_info.crossImplementation: besu-eth/besu's evmtool, EXECUTED, at fdf1247c6d (branch main), version 26.8-develop. A Java implementation sharing no code with go-ethereum, and configured by a FORK NAME rather than by a config fragment -- the same rule set under two representations, which this suite already records as stronger evidence than two clients sharing a shape. 12 of 12 gas figures and 12 of 12 return payloads agree.
_info.besuReportsNoOutcomeVOCABULARY: evmtool emits `pass`, which is TRUE for a revert -- it means the run completed, not that it succeeded. So besu corroborates `gasUsed` and `returnData` and says nothing about the `outcome` field; that half rests on go-ethereum and on the transcription below.
_info.independentTranscription: Every figure was computed a third time in Python from the rule as the specification states it -- VERY_LOW 3, the memory-expansion function `3*words + words**2//512`, and REVERT charging memory alone -- with arbitrary-precision integers. 12 of 12 agree. This is a transcription of a formula and NOT a third execution: it catches an implementation drifting from the document and cannot catch the document being wrong.
_info.theRULESETNAMESareLOCALandTHATISTHEPOINT: `withEip140` and `withoutEip140` are defined by the journals under `ruleSets`, inside this file. They borrow no network's upgrade label, which is what would have made this a network fixture wearing a component's directory. A harness resolves a vector by looking the name up here, never in a schedule.
_info.theJOURNALisORDEREDandISNOTASET: `proposals` is the list of proposals ADOPTED, in order, following the client's own model -- a proposal can be adopted, withdrawn and re-adopted on a live chain, so membership is not a question this list answers. Nothing in this file needs that distinction today; it is stated so a later suite does not quietly turn the field into a set.
_info.neitherOracleCanActivateOneProposalAlone: This is the real limit on the minimal pair and it is stated rather than smoothed over. go-ethereum's chain config has no per-proposal switch inside Byzantium and besu's evmtool takes a fork name, so the smallest step either can make is the whole upgrade -- nine proposals, not one. The attribution to EIP-140 rests on TWO things instead: the control pair `return_is_unchanged_by_the_proposal_when_present`/`_when_absent`, which is identical across the same step and so shows the step alone changes nothing; and the bodies containing none of the other EVM-visible members of that upgrade. Verified by walking the bytecode with PUSH data skipped: no 0x3d or 0x3e (EIP-211) and no 0xfa (EIP-214) in any body, with the walk calibrated against a probe that does carry a matching opcode. EIP-100, EIP-649 and EIP-658 are outside the machine entirely, and EIP-196, EIP-197 and EIP-198 are precompiles no body calls.
_info.aSINGLEPROPOSALPAIRisREACHABLEandTHISSUI: Recorded so the limit above is not read as permanent. The Parity-lineage chainspec carries PER-PROPOSAL activation keys, and `eip140Transition` is load-bearing in two implementations held here: openethereum/openethereum sets `schedule.have_revert = block_number >= self.eip140_transition` and gates the opcode on it, and NethermindEth/nethermind sets `releaseSpec.IsEip140Enabled` from the same key. So a rule set differing from its neighbour by EXACTLY EIP-140 is constructible, and this suite does not use one -- it uses two oracles that cannot express it, and carries the control-plus-bytecode-walk attribution instead. A later suite whose subject shares an upgrade with a proposal its bodies COULD reach should use that lineage rather than inherit this weaker form. REACHED 2026-08-30, and by a lineage neither this key nor the format doc named: core-geth's own chain config carries per-proposal activation keys of the same kind, and unlike either Parity-lineage client it is executable on this machine. The EIP-1052 suite's minimal pair is two core-geth genesis files differing by exactly one JSON key. Nothing about THIS file changed as a result -- its values stand and its weaker attribution is still the honest statement of how they were produced -- but a later suite should reach for that route, and the canary it needs is in FIXTURE-FORMAT.md.
_info.chainIdIsNOTAnInputAndTHATWASMEASURED: The whole set was regenerated at chain id 61 and every result is identical. So is a run at timestamp 1,700,000,000, and one with the coinbase and difficulty changed. Calibrated in the other direction: removing byzantiumBlock from both rule sets DIFFERS on exactly the four REVERT vectors, so a run of IDENTICALs is a measurement rather than a broken comparison.
_info.heightCOULDNOTBEMEASUREDandTHATISTHESEAM: `evm run` panics on a genesis carrying `number > 0` (`can't commit genesis block with number > 0`, core/genesis.go), so height cannot be varied through it. The claim is carried structurally instead: this file has no height field for a vector to key on, and no body contains BLOCKHASH, NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, DIFFICULTY, GASLIMIT, CHAINID or any state-reading opcode -- the same calibrated walk cited above.
_info.aHALTEDVECTORSgasUsedRESTATESTHEBUDGET: An exceptional halt consumes everything, so on those five vectors `gasUsed` EQUALS `gasBudget` by definition and asserts nothing on its own. What those vectors assert is the `outcome` and the `halt`. Two of them exist purely to make that visible: `revert_undefined_consumes_the_whole_budget` runs the same body at five times the budget and the figure follows it, while `revert_gas_does_not_depend_on_the_budget` does the same to a revert and the figure does not move.
_info.callValueISAREALINPUTandTHERESTARENOT: Measured: changing the caller, the receiver or the calldata leaves every result identical, and a non-zero call value does NOT -- go-ethereum answers `insufficient balance for transfer` at gas 0, because no account here is funded. Every vector therefore states `callValue` explicitly at zero rather than leaving it to a default.
_info.twoINSTRUMENTTRAPSFOUNDWHILEGENERATING: Both return a confident wrong answer rather than an error. (1) besu's evmtool SILENTLY falls back to its newest fork when it does not recognise a `--fork` name: `--fork=SpuriousDragon` in four spellings ran BPO5, exactly as a deliberately invented name did, and the first pass read as besu disagreeing with go-ethereum about pre-adoption REVERT. The generator now reads back the `fork` field evmtool echoes and refuses a run whose echo does not match. (2) go-ethereum's `--gas` flag is INERT whenever `--prestate` carries a non-zero `gasLimit`, which the genesis then supplies instead; the budget in this file is set through the genesis for that reason.
_info.wrongBuildMethod: Five defects were introduced into go-ethereum one at a time, each confirmed to change the source and compile, with the unmodified build as a control. The reference clone was NEVER mutated: every defect is a `go build -overlay` replacement of one file, so a clean clone is a property of the method rather than of a restore step somebody could skip. `git status --porcelain` in the clone returned zero lines afterwards. A patch whose anchor text is not found raises rather than building an unchanged binary, because a build that silently applied nothing would score 12/12 and read exactly like a coverage gap.

wrongBuildScores.revert_consumes_all_gas_like_a_halt: 8/12 -- fails every REVERT vector and no other. Routing ErrExecutionReverted through the halt exit instead of the revert exit; the failure this proposal exists to distinguish from an exceptional one.
wrongBuildScores.revert_is_available_before_it_was_adopte: 10/12 -- fails exactly the two `withoutEip140` REVERT vectors. THIS IS THE SCORE THAT MAKES THE RULE-SET FIELD LOAD-BEARING: registering the operation in the Homestead instruction set changes nothing a single-rule-set fixture could see, and this file catches it because the same body is asserted under two stated journals.
wrongBuildScores.revert_does_not_pay_for_the_memory_it_na: 1 of 12 -- and the narrowness is the point rather than a weakness. Only `revert_pays_for_the_memory_it_names` names a range wider than the memory already in use; in every other REVERT vector the memory was expanded by an earlier MSTORE or not at all, so REVERT's own expansion charge is genuinely zero there and a build that skips it is not wrong at those vectors. One vector exists for exactly this defect.
wrongBuildScores.revert_hands_back_no_payload: 9/12 -- fails the three vectors whose revert payload is non-empty, and correctly passes `revert_with_an_empty_payload_is_still_a_revert`, whose payload is empty in a correct build too.
wrongBuildScores.an_exceptional_halt_keeps_its_remaining_: 7/12 -- fails all five halted vectors. The mirror of the first defect, and the reason the `invalid_opcode_halts_*` and `out_of_gas_*` vectors are here: without them a build could return gas from every failure and still pass everything this file asserts about REVERT.

invocationContext.comment: The frame every vector runs in. Stated because it is not derivable from the vectors and a reader guessing differently gets different gas.
invocationContext.codeIsDeployedAtTheCalleeNotExecutedAsIn: Each `code` is the callee's deployed code and the invocation is a CALL, never a CREATE. Running it as initcode charges a deposit per byte and asserts something else entirely.
invocationContext.callerAndCalleeAreNOTInputs: MEASURED: the two oracles used different defaults for both and agree on all twelve vectors, and setting them explicitly in go-ethereum changes nothing.
invocationContext.noAccountIsFunded: Which is why every `callValue` is zero -- see `_info.callValueISAREALINPUTandTHERESTARENOT`. Every vector now STATES that, as `"pre": {}`, rather than leaving it to this note: the shape gained a required `pre` field with the EIP-1052 suite, and an empty map is the assertion that no account exists. No expectation moved when it was added -- all twelve were re-generated through both oracles on 2026-08-30 and are byte-identical.

withoutEip140.comment: A rule set that has not adopted the proposal. The name is LOCAL to this file and is defined by the journal below, not by any network's word for an upgrade.

generatedWith.go-ethereum: a genesis chain config carrying homesteadBlock 0 and nothing later

withoutEip140.widerSetsWereMEASUREDToGiveTheSameAnswer: Widening this to Spurious Dragon in go-ethereum (adding eip150Block, eip155Block and eip158Block at 0) leaves all twelve results byte-identical, so nothing here turns on stopping at Homestead. Homestead is stated because it is the one pre-adoption set BOTH oracles can address: besu's evmtool has no name for Spurious Dragon.

withEip140.comment: The same journal with the proposal adopted, plus the rest of the upgrade that carried it. The extra members are listed because they were genuinely in force during generation -- see `_info.neitherOracleCanActivateOneProposalAlone`.

generatedWith.go-ethereum: a genesis chain config carrying homesteadBlock, eip150Block, eip155Block, eip158Block and byzantiumBlock, all at 0

vectors.name: revert_returns_its_payload_and_keeps_the_unspent_gas
vectors.comment: THE SUBJECT. The invocation fails, the caller gets the bytes it named, and all but 18 gas comes back.

vectors.name: revert_gas_does_not_depend_on_the_budget
vectors.comment: DISCRIMINATOR against a build that treats REVERT as consuming everything: five times the budget, the same 18 gas.

vectors.name: revert_with_an_empty_payload_is_still_a_revert
vectors.comment: No memory is touched, so only the two pushes are paid for. Separates 'reverted with no data' from 'halted'.

vectors.name: revert_pays_for_the_memory_it_names
vectors.comment: The proposal's own words: the contract 'only has to pay for memory'. Naming 64 bytes never written costs 6 more than naming none.

vectors.name: revert_opcode_is_undefined_without_the_proposal
vectors.comment: MINIMAL PAIR with the first vector: the same body, one proposal absent. 0xfd is not an operation, so the frame halts and keeps nothing.

vectors.name: revert_undefined_consumes_the_whole_budget
vectors.comment: PAIRS WITH revert_gas_does_not_depend_on_the_budget. Here gasUsed DOES track the budget, which is what an exceptional halt means.

vectors.name: return_is_unchanged_by_the_proposal_when_present
vectors.comment: CONTROL. Same body shape, RETURN instead of REVERT.

vectors.name: return_is_unchanged_by_the_proposal_when_absent
vectors.comment: CONTROL, and the one that carries the attribution: identical to the vector above at both rule sets, so the difference the pair above measures is EIP-140 and not another member of the same upgrade.

vectors.name: invalid_opcode_halts_when_the_proposal_is_present
vectors.comment: 0xfe halts at both rule sets. Adopting EIP-140 does not soften an exceptional halt.

vectors.name: invalid_opcode_halts_when_the_proposal_is_absent
vectors.comment: The answer revert_opcode_is_undefined_without_the_proposal gives, reached by an opcode that is undefined at EVERY rule set -- so that vector is not a special case.

vectors.name: stop_costs_nothing_at_either_rule_set
vectors.comment: CALIBRATION. The gas field can report zero, so a zero elsewhere is a measurement rather than an unrun probe.

vectors.name: out_of_gas_is_a_halt_and_not_a_revert
vectors.comment: DISCRIMINATOR on the halt reason: the same body that reverts at 100000 cannot afford its own PUSH32 at 10. Both are failures; only one keeps gas.
